source.title: Redundant Attention Heads in Large Language Models For In Context Learning

record.tranche_reason: The post applies attention-head ablations and activation patching to examine compensatory behavior, but uses a narrow in-context arithmetic task and qualitative measures rather than the original study's measure.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative outcomes from ablations, patching, and attention-pattern observations. Its Bayesian-update account and proposed MLP subtask mechanism are hypotheses or arguments, not additional reported tests of the claim. It does not report numeric effect sizes.
record.test_reason: The post ablates whole attention layers in llama-3-8b. It reports that the answer stays correct, that task formation (located by patching) moves to later layers, and that later-layer heads activate strongly. This bears directly on V1, using a different method (patch-point localization, qualitative) on a narrow in-context arithmetic task.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that llama-3-8b has many redundant attention heads for this in-context task, with later-layer backup heads taking over when earlier layers are ablated. The author takes this as weak support for induction heads driving in-context learning. The Bayesian feature-addition and MLP-subtask accounts are offered with lower confidence and without direct tests.
record.recipe_differences: Uses attention-head ablation and residual-stream activation patching, but studies a narrow arithmetic in-context task and reports qualitative answers, patch points, and attention patterns rather than a quantitative comparison of direct and total output effects.
record.method_sensitivity: The patch point associated with the task representation shifts depending on which layer is ablated: layers 10 and 11 shift it from layer 12 to before layer 14; ablating layer 13 shifts it to before layer 16; after ablating layer 15, the patching behavior differs.

fits_no_version.finding: After layer 15 is ablated, patching at no layer yields the ≈2x task behaviour; instead it transfers almost the exact answer from Model A.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The patching behaviour used to localize an in-context task representation can change qualitatively with the ablated layer.

record.problems: Evidence is qualitative and limited to one model and one narrow arithmetic task. No numerical effect sizes, uncertainty estimates, or explicit control comparisons are reported. The ablation type is unspecified, and backup-head involvement is inferred from attention patterns rather than tested by ablating those heads.

untested.parts: Late-MLP downregulation of the maximum-likelihood token and its change under ablation are not examined.
No single-head ablations, no general text, and only one model family and size.
No average compensation fraction, no prompt-level variance, and no overcorrection measure; there is only one example prompt.
Backup heads are named from attention patterns only and are not causally tested. Copy-suppression heads, LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure neurons are not examined.
The ablation type is not specified.
No ablation-based importance scores are computed or compared.

missing.what: After ablating layers 10–11, backup heads on layer 13 'activate very strongly'. This is attention-pattern evidence of downstream compensation and has no row.
The heads contributing most in each ablated layer had attention patterns matching the author's proposed subtask algorithm. This is qualitative.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is anecdotal: one prompt, one model, unspecified ablation type, no numbers. The post frames the result as redundancy rather than self-repair. An unchanged answer alone cannot separate active compensation from redundancy, but the shifting patch point and the strong later-head activation point toward downstream compensation. It is unclear whether successive layer ablations are cumulative.

versions.untested_parts: No quantitative comparison of an ablated component's direct effect with the total output effect; compensation is tested only in one arithmetic in-context task and one model.
Late MLP downregulation of the maximum-likelihood token and its change under earlier ablations are not tested.
The post ablates groups of heads in layers, not single heads, and does not test general text, multiple model families, or multiple sizes.
It does not measure average compensation, prompt-to-prompt variability, or overcorrection.
It points to backup heads from attention patterns, but does not causally test individual heads or test copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons.
The ablation type is not specified as mean, resample, or zero ablation.
No ablation-based importance score is measured or compared with another attribution measure.

tranche.reason: Attention-head ablation, residual-stream patch-point localization and qualitative attention-pattern observations address later-layer compensation using a different method and measure.

source_check.notes: No numerical compensation magnitude or ablation replacement type is reported; preserved answers do not quantify restoration of the output distribution. Early patching transfers only an approximate y≈2x task, and cumulative ablation status is unspecified.

statements.correction: Unmodified first working patch point: layer 12. After layers 10–11 ablation: before layer 14. Following layer-13 ablation: shift from 14 to 16. Retention of the earlier ablations: not explicitly specified.
statements.problem: The patch-point numbers are correct, but also ablating layer 13 presents the cumulative design as explicit; the text only implies it.

statements.correction: Layer-13 ablation: reported patch-point shift from 14 to 16; cumulative ablation status unspecified. Candidate backup heads: identified through attention patterns. Individual heads' causal contributions and fraction of compensation carried: unmeasured.
statements.problem: The cumulative layer-13 ablation is implied rather than explicit. Tested on V5 overstates the evidence for identifiable heads carrying compensation.
